items.tr: Fince'de fiil kişiye göre çekimlenir: "ben" = olen, "o" = on. Bu yüzden "minä on" yanlıştır. Çekim kişiyi zaten gösterdiği için "minä" genelde söylenmez: "Olen opettaja."
items.en: Finnish verbs change their ending for each person: "I am" = olen, "he/she is" = on, so "minä on" is wrong. Because "olen" already means "I am", "minä" is usually dropped.
You want to know their name.
You want to know their job.
You want to make sure you understand each other.
What do you do for work?

items.tr: Fince'de "daha büyük" gibi karşılaştırma sıfatın sonuna -mpi eki eklenerek yapılır: iso (büyük) -> isompi (daha büyük).
items.en: To say "bigger", Finnish adds -mpi to the adjective instead of using a separate word: iso (big) becomes isompi (bigger).
items.context: Onko teillä tätä isommassa koossa? / ✗ Onko teillä tätä iso koossa?

items.en: You pick up a piece of clothing.
You do not like the color.
You look for a better price.

items.tr: Bunun daha büyük bedeni var mı?
items.en: Do you have this in a bigger size?
Is this available in another color?

items.tr: Birden büyük sayılardan sonra isim çoğul olmaz, özel bir ek alır: "kaksi lasta" (iki çocuk) derken "lapset" değil "lasta" kullanılır.
items.en: After a number greater than one, the noun changes its ending instead of becoming plural: "kaksi lasta" (two children) uses "lasta", not "lapset".
items.context: Minulla on kaksi lasta. / ✗ Minulla on kaksi lapset.

items.en: You want to know the time.
You tell a friend the price.
Someone asks how many children you have.
You count the animals you see.

items.tr: İyelik ("benim") ayrı bir kelimeyle değil, ismin sonuna eklenen -ni ekiyle gösterilir: äiti (anne) -> äitini (annem).
items.en: Possession is shown by adding -ni to the end of the noun instead of a separate word for "my": äiti (mother) becomes äitini (my mother).
items.context: Tässä on äitini. / ✗ Tässä on minun äiti.

items.en: They ask if you have siblings.
They ask where your brother lives.
You ask them the same question.
My sister is younger than me.
My parents live in the countryside.

items.tr: Hava durumu cümlelerinde İngilizce'deki "it" gibi bir özne kullanılmaz, sadece "on" fiili ve sıfat yeterlidir.
items.en: Weather sentences use only "on" plus an adjective, with no subject word like English "it".
items.context: Ulkona on kylmä. / ✗ Se on kylmä ulkona.

items.en: You look up at the sky.
You warn a friend before they leave.

items.tr: Bir yere gitmek/varmak anlamı isim sonuna -lle eki eklenerek verilir: asema (istasyon) -> asemalle (istasyona).
items.en: To say you are going "to" a place, add -lle to the end of the noun: asema (station) becomes asemalle (to the station).
items.context: Haluan mennä lentokentälle. / ✗ Haluan mennä lentokenttä.

items.en: You are lost near a train station.
They ask how you get to work.
You are not sure you are in the right place.
You are heading to catch a flight.
How do I get to the station?
I go to work by bus.
Where do I buy a ticket?
The next train leaves at nine o'clock.
I want to go to the airport.

items.tr: Emir kipi, fiilin sözlük halinden -a/-ä harfinin atılmasıyla yapılır: soittaa (aramak) -> soita (ara!).
items.en: The command form drops the final -a/-ä from the dictionary form of the verb: soittaa (to call) becomes soita (call!).
You need someone who can translate.

items.tr: "Ben" özneli fiiller -n ekiyle biter: herää + n = herään.
items.en: Verbs used with "I" end in -n: herää + n = herään (I wake up).
items.context: Herään kello seitsemän. / ✗ Herää kello seitsemän.

items.en: They ask when you leave the house.
They ask about your morning habits.
They ask what you do before bed.
They ask if your days are different.
I wake up at seven o'clock.
I leave home at eight o'clock.
I take a shower every morning.
I read a book before going to bed.
I go to sleep at eleven o'clock.
I do the same things every day.
Telling a story about your day

items.tr: Geçmiş zaman, fiil gövdesine -i- eklenerek yapılır: mennä (gitmek) -> menin (gittim).
items.en: The past tense is made by adding -i- inside the verb: mennä (to go) becomes menin (I went).
items.context: Eilen menin kaupunkiin. / ✗ Menen kaupunkiin eilen.

items.en: Someone asks what you did yesterday.
They ask if you saw anyone.
They ask what you did together.
They ask about the weather that day.
They ask when you got home.
They ask how the day was.
Yesterday I went to the city.
I met my friend at a café.
Then we walked in the park.
I returned home in the evening.
